name: Fraud — Authorized Push-Payment (APP) / social-engineering scams
category: Currently-stated (README) target, expanded — fraud detection where the legitimate account-holder is socially engineered
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Authorized Push Payment (APP) / social-engineering scam detection on real-time payment rails (UK Faster Payments, SEPA Instant, FedNow, RTP, AU NPP, SG FAST, IN UPI).
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A bank's fraud/payments risk engine must score every outbound real-time transfer within the few-hundred-millisecond authorization window and decide hold/step-up/release before the funds are irrevocably committed on the rail.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Score every outbound Faster-Payments / instant-rail transfer in <100 ms using per-payer + per-(payer,counterparty) + per-counterparty velocity, first-time-payee, large-amount-relative-to-history, and behavioral session features. 2) Detect 'social engineering in progress' from session-level signals (long typing pauses on the recipient field, copy-paste of sort code / account number, phone-on-ear via device sensors, call correlation) and elevate risk for the next authorized payment. 3) Identify probable mule receiving accounts on the inbound leg (sudden inbound velocity from new payers, rapid forward-out, low account age) since UK PSR splits liability 50/50 with the receiving PSP since Oct 7 2024.
domain_fit.event_shapes: (a) payment_initiated {payment_id, payer_account, counterparty_account, counterparty_sort_code, amount, currency, channel(web|mobile|open-banking), CoP_result, ts}; (b) session_signal {session_id, user_id, event(typing_pause|copy_paste|focus_lost|sensor_proximity|call_active), payload, ts}; (c) cop_lookup {payer, counterparty, match|close|no_match, ts}; (d) payment_authorized / payment_settled / payment_reversed; (e) inbound_credit {beneficiary_account, payer_bank, amount, ts}; (f) call_signal (from Scam Signal / telco partnership) {user_msisdn, in_call_with_unknown, call_duration, ts}.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Counts and sums: count(outbound, payer, [1m,10m,1h,24h,7d]); sum(outbound_amount, payer, …); count_distinct(counterparty, payer, [24h,30d]). Per-pair velocity: count(payment, (payer,counterparty), [24h,30d]) → first_time_payee flag = (count==1). Amount distributions: percentile_rank(amount, distribution(payer_outbound_amount, 90d)); z-score(amount, mean/std payer-outbound, 90d). Inbound (mule): count_distinct(payer_bank, beneficiary, 24h); rate(forward_out_amount / inbound_amount, beneficiary, 24h); time_since_first_credit(beneficiary). Session: count(copy_paste_recipient, session, session-window); sum(typing_pause_ms, session, session-window); rate(field_corrections, session). Peer-group: distance(payer_amount_distribution, peer_group_distribution).
domain_fit.entity_grain: Primary keys are heterogeneous and must coexist: payer_account_id, counterparty_account_id, (payer_account_id, counterparty_account_id) pair, session_id (per device session), beneficiary_account_id (inbound/mule side), and msisdn for telco call-correlation features.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Mixed. Sliding windows are mandatory for velocities (1 m / 10 m / 1 h / 24 h / 7 d / 30 d / 90 d) — exact counts are preferable but HLL is acceptable for count_distinct(counterparty) at >30 d horizons. Session windows are required for behavioral features (typing/copy-paste/dwell aggregations gated on session start/inactivity timeout). Tumbling windows (e.g. daily peer-group recomputes) feed offline baselines.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: Idempotent at-least-once is acceptable for velocity features (small duplicate count drift does not change decisions materially) but the durable fraud-decision audit trail must be exactly-once / regulator-grade — every score and feature snapshot at decision time must be replayable for PSR / FOS dispute resolution under the Oct-2024 mandatory reimbursement regime.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Sub-100 ms feature-fetch + score. UK Faster Payments end-to-end SLA is ~20 s, but the fraud decision must fit inside an internal <2-3 s envelope that includes CoP, AML screening, and core-banking debit; the feature-store slice is typically budgeted at <50 ms p99.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Sub-second for outbound transaction velocities and session signals (the previous click and the next payment can be milliseconds apart in instant rails); <5 s acceptable for inbound mule features; minutes acceptable for slow-moving peer-group baselines.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: UK Faster Payments cleared ~5.0 bn payments in 2024 (~160 EPS sustained system-wide, with peaks well above that on payday Fridays). A tier-1 UK bank typically handles 10–30 % of FPS volume → steady-state ~15–50 outbound EPS per bank but peak bursts of thousands of EPS during salary/bill runs; multiply by ~10× for inbound credits + session signals + CoP lookups feeding the same engine. beava's published ~684k EPS single-core on M4 (TCP+msgpack, parallel=16) is two orders of magnitude above what a single tier-1 PSP needs for the payment leg alone, so headroom is comfortable. [uncertain]
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Roughly balanced to slightly read-heavy at decision time: each outbound payment writes ~5–20 feature updates (counters across windows) and reads 50–200 features for the score. Inbound credits and session signals are write-heavy with no synchronous read.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Tier-1 UK retail bank ~25–30 M active customer accounts × O(few KB) of feature state per (account × window-bucket × counterparty-pair tail) ≈ 100–300 GB hot state. (payer,counterparty) pair cardinality is the long tail — a customer with 50 distinct payees over 90 days × 30 M accounts ≈ 1.5 B pairs at O(100 B) each ≈ 150 GB just for the per-pair feature. This is at or above what beava's in-memory-only model comfortably fits on a single node; sharding or per-tenant horizontal partitioning would be required. [uncertain]
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Three regimes: (a) slowly-growing — payer accounts (bounded by retail customer base); (b) explosive — sessions, devices, msisdns and (payer,counterparty) pairs (the pair space grows with payment history); (c) bounded but adversarial — receiving mule accounts churn rapidly as fraud rings burn them.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Hot session features: minutes to hours. Velocity features: 1 m / 10 m / 1 h / 24 h / 7 d / 30 d / 90 d windows. Audit/decision snapshots: 6 years (FCA/PRA record-retention) to indefinite for PSR-disputed APP claims.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 50–200 features per payment scoring request is typical for production APP scoring (Stripe's Radar reportedly scans >1,000 characteristics per transaction; bank fraud engines like Lloyds DRE and Featurespace ARIC fall in the same envelope). beava's batch_get is the right shape for this — a single decision should be one round-trip.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Regulator-grade for the decision audit trail (PSR mandatory reimbursement requires firms to evidence the controls applied to every disputed transaction; FCA SYSC and CP/PS25/5 require demonstrable model governance). The live feature state itself can tolerate WAL+snapshot recovery as long as in-flight payments either re-replay or fail-safe; beava's WAL+periodic-snapshot story is acceptable for the feature plane but the scoring decisions and feature snapshots used at decision time should be persisted out-of-band to a regulator-grade log.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Regional single-binary fits well at small/mid PSP scale (challenger banks, EMIs, payment processors). Tier-1 banks need multi-region active-active for DR and cannot tolerate a single-node failure domain for live payment decisioning — beava's lack of in-process sharding and replication in v0 is the blocking gap here.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Bank fraud / financial-crime risk team (the 'Head of Fraud' or 'Head of Payment Risk'), with the ML / data-platform team as the technical sponsor. In challenger banks and EMIs the same team owns both. Secondary buyers: payments-processor risk teams (ClearBank, Form3, Modulr-style) and telco-bank consortia (Scam Signal participants).
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Strong and regulator-driven. UK APP-fraud losses were £450.7 m in 2024 (UK Finance Annual Fraud Report 2025); UK PSPs paid £173 m in mandatory reimbursement between Oct 2024 and Sept 2025 (first full year of the PSR regime). The fraud-and-financial-crime detection software market that this funds is estimated at $25–40 B globally with Featurespace (acquired by Visa for ~$1 B in 2024), NICE Actimize, Feedzai, BioCatch, ThreatMark, and Hawk AI as named beneficiaries. Australia's Scams Prevention Framework (passed Feb 2025) and Singapore's Shared Responsibility Framework (Dec 16 2024) extend the regulatory pull to APAC.
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) UK PSR mandatory reimbursement (effective 7 Oct 2024) — sending and receiving PSPs split the cost 50/50 up to £85 k per claim, which makes inbound mule detection a brand-new line-item for receiving banks. 2) Australia Scams Prevention Framework (Feb 2025) creates administrative penalties for banks/telcos/platforms lacking controls. 3) Singapore SRF (Dec 16 2024) allocates liability between banks and telcos. 4) Rising APP loss rates on instant rails globally — instant-payment channels are reported to account for >90 % of APP losses by value. 5) Pay.UK RCMS compliance deadline (1 May 2025) for direct FPS participants.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: UK FCA SYSC + PSR PS24/7 + PS25/5 (APP reimbursement); Pay.UK Faster Payments scheme rules; FCA Consumer Duty (vulnerable customers); GDPR (behavioral telemetry is personal data — typing rhythm and device sensors are biometric-adjacent); EU PSD3/PSR1 proposals extending IBAN-name verification across SEPA; AU Scams Prevention Framework; MAS SRF + TRM guidelines. Implication for beava: PII flows through the event stream (account numbers, sort codes, msisdns), so TLS-on-the-wire and at-rest encryption are hard requirements that v0 does not yet provide.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Realistic prototype in 2–4 weeks: a beava deployment ingesting synthetic FPS-shaped payment events and emitting per-payer, per-pair, and first-time-payee features for a downstream scorer can be stood up by one engineer in days; integration with a real bank's payment switch and audit-grade evidencing extends this to months. The deepest blocker for a production design-partner deal is TLS+auth, not the data model.

competition.incumbents: Generic streaming/feature-store stack: Redis (often Redis Enterprise) + Lua for online counters; Apache Flink / Kafka Streams for windowed aggregations feeding a serving store; Tecton, Feast, Chalk and Fennel as managed feature platforms; Aerospike and RonDB as low-latency online stores; DragonflyDB as a Redis-compatible challenger.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Domain-specific incumbents are the named risk engines: Featurespace ARIC Scam Detect (NatWest reported 135 % scam-detection lift, 75 % FP reduction; ClearBank deployment; acquired by Visa in 2024); NICE Actimize IFM-X / X-Sight; Feedzai (TrustScore / Feedzai IQ network intelligence); Hawk AI; BioCatch Scams360 (behavioral biometrics — typing/copy-paste/dwell signals); ThreatMark; SAS Fraud Management; ACI Worldwide ReD; Mastercard Consumer Fraud Risk (the nine-UK-bank consortium). On the mule/inbound side: SymphonyAI / Quantexa for network resolution. None of these are sold as a developer-facing feature server — they bundle ingestion, models, case management and analytics.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single binary, Apache-2.0, no broker required — fits the challenger-bank / EMI architecture where the payment switch can push directly over TCP+msgpack without standing up Kafka+Flink+Redis. 2) 50+ aggregation primitives natively (counters, velocities, distances, distributions) means many APP features are declarative `@bv.table` calls rather than custom Flink jobs. 3) Sub-millisecond batch_get fits the 50-ms feature-fetch budget with room to spare and beats Redis+Lua for complex windowed counters. 4) The (payer, counterparty) pair-grain feature — which is awkward in Redis+Lua and slow in a generic SQL feature store — is a first-class entity in beava. 5) No open-core wall: a fraud team can self-host without per-decision licence fees that Featurespace / Actimize charge.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS on the wire and no authentication on :8080/:8081/:8090 — instant blocker for any regulated PSP. 2) No in-process sharding or replication — a tier-1 bank cannot run live payment scoring on a single failure-domain node. 3) In-memory only with refuse-on-network-FS — fine for a sidecar but limits state to one box; the long-tail (payer,counterparty) pair space at tier-1 scale (~1.5 B pairs, ~150 GB+) is awkward. 4) No triggers — APP detection often needs 'fire when velocity crosses threshold' (e.g. step-up to face-biometric confirmation, hand off to call-back queue); today this has to be polled. 5) No audit-grade decision log out of the box — feature snapshots used at decision time must be persisted externally for PSR/FOS replay. 6) No native handling for behavioral session signals as a separate entity type with session-window semantics (must be modelled with explicit session keys). 7) No multi-tenancy / no per-customer-segment RBAC for use inside a bank.
competition.integration_surface: In a typical PSP architecture beava would sit between the payment switch / API gateway and the model-scoring service. Upstream producers are typically the payment orchestrator (push via TCP/HTTP), the mobile/web SDK (session signals, possibly via a session-collector service rather than direct push), and the CoP/AML services. Downstream consumers are the ML scorer (XGBoost/LightGBM/Featurespace's ANN) and rules engines. This 'push-not-pull' shape is well aligned with how risk teams already operate (events flow into the engine; decisions flow out) and is different from Kafka-only Feast/Tecton designs that assume Kafka as the only ingress.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Banks typically combine a deterministic rules engine (Drools, in-house DSL, or the vendor's rule language) for hard limits and regulatory cut-offs with one or more ML scorers (XGBoost/LightGBM gradient-boosted trees, increasingly graph-neural / sequence models for mule networks). beava's role is upstream of both — it serves the feature vector; the model lives elsewhere.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No public beava deployment for APP fraud is known. Comparable public references on competing stacks: NatWest on Featurespace ARIC (135 % scam-detection improvement); ClearBank on Featurespace; the nine-UK-bank Mastercard Consumer Fraud Risk consortium (Lloyds, Halifax, BoS, NatWest, Monzo, TSB and others); Lloyds Banking Group's proprietary Dynamic Risk Engine; Featurespace Scam Detect general launch covering UK Faster Payments. [uncertain]
adoption_signals.community_discussions: No beava-specific GitHub issues or Discord threads on APP fraud have surfaced in public search as of May 2026. Broader community signal is strong: UK Finance Annual Fraud Report 2025, PSR PS25/5 (May 2025), Pay.UK RCMS rollout (May 2025), and a continuous stream of ThreatMark/BioCatch/Featurespace blog content on PSR compliance lessons-learned. [uncertain]
adoption_signals.examples_or_demos_in_repo: No APP-fraud vertical demo currently shipped in the beava repository (no `examples/app_fraud/` or similar directory observed at the time of research). A demo would be high-value: a Python script declaring `@bv.event payment_initiated`, `@bv.table(key=payer)` velocity tables, `@bv.table(key=(payer,counterparty))` pair tables, and a notebook that scores synthetic FPS-shaped traffic. [uncertain]
adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: High and rising. APP fraud is an actively-adversarial domain — fraud rings rotate mule accounts, rotate scripts, exploit each new rail (FedNow, RTP, UPI) within months of launch, and adapt to public rules (CoP-evading accounts that yield positive name matches are already documented by Pay.UK). Models retrain on weekly-to-monthly cadence; concept drift is the default state.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) Long historical lookback / batch backfill — anything older than ~90 d of velocities belongs in an offline lakehouse (Snowflake/Databricks/Iceberg), not in beava. 2) Multi-entity graph joins — mule-network detection across millions of accounts is a graph-DB (Neo4j, TigerGraph, Quantexa) or graph-neural-network problem, not a feature-server one. 3) Full event archive — beava is not the regulator-grade audit log; that must live in S3/object-store with WORM retention. 4) Case management — PSR claim workflow, FOS escalation and reimbursement disbursement are vendor / in-house ops tools, not beava. 5) The ML model itself — beava serves the features; the scorer is XGBoost/LightGBM/etc.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Production-blocking: (a) TLS termination on :8080/:8081 and mutual-TLS or token auth on :8090 admin — without these no UK or EU bank can run beava inside a regulated payment flow; (b) authenticated multi-tenant API surface (RBAC per team / per environment); (c) replication and at-least-one secondary read replica with automated failover so a single-node WAL+snapshot crash does not stop payment scoring; (d) horizontal sharding by entity key for the (payer,counterparty) long tail; (e) triggers / 'fire-on-threshold-crossed' so APP step-up flows can be event-driven rather than polled; (f) per-decision feature-snapshot export (a compact, signed record of every feature value seen by the scorer at decision time) for PSR / FOS replay; (g) at-rest encryption for hot state, since account numbers and msisdns are PII; (h) graceful eviction / TTL on the long-tail (payer,counterparty) pair grain; (i) first-class session-window semantics for behavioral signals (typing pauses, copy-paste events) including idle-timeout based session expiry; (j) Confirmation-of-Payee enrichment helpers (treat CoP result as a first-class event type) and ISO 20022 pacs.008 event templates.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes — production APP detection wants both. (1) Synchronous feature-serving for every payment-initiated request (which beava handles today). (2) Event-driven actions: when (count(outbound,payer,1h) crosses N) OR (first-time-payee==true AND amount > p99(payer,90d)) OR (typing_pause_sum,session > T), fire an out-of-band step-up (face-biometric, in-app confirmation, branch call-back) or hard-hold the payment. v0 beava has no trigger primitive; today this would require polling the relevant counters from the scoring service and acting in the application layer.
